fatal_errors: The hypothesis replaces the target AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating on SS316L with chromium short-range ordering in uncoated conventional steels.
It omits atmospheric plasma spraying, the approximately 150 µm coating, the 550 °C optimum anneal, and the comparison with as-sprayed and uncoated SS316L.

Neither cited paper provides evidence that chromium short-range ordering improves corrosion resistance or promotes self-healing Cr-rich passive films; the evidence concerns dislocation behavior and mechanical strengthening.

The proposed annealing comparison cannot attribute corrosion changes specifically to short-range ordering because annealing may also alter grain size, segregation, precipitates, residual stress, and surface condition.
The claimed scope across stainless steels, low-alloy steels, acidic or saline solutions, and reactor primary water is much broader than either the cited evidence or the target experiments support.
explanation: The response addresses corrosion resistance in application-relevant steels and proposes measurable electrochemical and microscopy tests, but it does not reconstruct the reported materials system or treatment. The target mechanism is associated with a plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating annealed at 550 °C, its refined and relatively dense microstructure, and formation of Al- and Cr-rich protective products in sulfuric acid and specified molten-salt exposures. The generated hypothesis instead assigns causality to Cr/Mo short-range ordering in the substrate. Its predicted lower corrosion current, weight loss, and improved passivation qualitatively overlap the target outcomes, but only at a generic level. The experiment would be more discriminating if SRO were independently varied while grain size, precipitation, residual stress, and surface finish were held constant, and if corrosion response correlated quantitatively with verified SRO. Most importantly, the cited studies do not test corrosion or passive-film formation, so they cannot support the asserted governing mechanism.
